annotations.target_phrase: the star leaving his fingers, flash of silver, to bury itself in the face of the wall screen
annotations.annotation_text: Case discarding his talisman by hurling the shuriken into the video monitor, symbolically severing his obsession with the lethal romanticism of the street.
sources: Gibson, William. Neuromancer. Ace Books, 1984, p. 290.

annotations.target_phrase: new pancreas and liver, the rest on a new Ono-Sendai and a ticket back to the Sprawl
annotations.annotation_text: Case's financial payout from the run: purchasing biological organ replacements to cure his toxic addiction, upgrading his cyberdeck, and returning to the Sprawl to resume life as a console cowboy.
sources: Gibson, William. Neuromancer. Ace Books, 1984, p. 290.

annotations.target_phrase: the boy’s grin, his pink gums, the glitter of the long gray eyes that had been Riviera’s... third figure was himself
annotations.annotation_text: The enigmatic concluding vision in the matrix: Case encounters Neuromancer, Linda Lee, and a digital construct of himself smiling eternally within the lattice of cyberspace light, achieving a paradoxical virtual immortality.
sources: Gibson, William. Neuromancer. Ace Books, 1984, p. 290.
Hayles, N. Katherine. How We Became Posthuman. (1999).

annotations.target_phrase: Somewhere, very close, the laugh that wasn’t laughter.
annotations.annotation_text: The haunting acoustic coda of the novel: the digital laugh of McCoy Pauley (the Dixie Flatline) lingering in the matrix, echoing the theme of consciousness persevering as pure algorithmic pattern.
sources: Gibson, William. Neuromancer. Ace Books, 1984, p. 290.
